title: Best free, self-hosted LLM and MCP client for Unity MCP?
author: One-Fall9946
selftext:
I've been working with Unity for a few years and would like to start exploring Unity MCP, particularly for experimenting with AI-assisted development and widening my horizons at first.

From what I understand, I need an LLM and an MCP client/agent to connect it to Unity. I've tried searching around, but I'm very new to the AI side of things and haven't quite figured out which options work best together.

Ideally, I'm looking for something that's:

* Free
* Self-hosted / runs locally
* Compatible with Unity MCP

What would you recommend for someone just getting started? Any advice would be appreciated!

I have 3060 TI if that matters.

comments.author: llamaGames12
comments.body: I totally recommend using the new CLI instead of the MCP, its so so much better imho!

replies.author: One-Fall9946
replies.body: I noticed some improvement with CLI over MCP although it still takes lot of time, attempts and adjustments to do something simple like create a cube. And then it fails when I ask it to build a simple house from primitive shapes. I presume my VRAM is just too low. I tried a bunch of models like qwen, gemma, bonbas, etc. What model do you use?

replies.author: llamaGames12
replies.body: thats quite strange, I mean just use CLI not MCP, it can not only create a cube but it can create a whole level (easily might I add), I'm using opus 5.5

comments.author: Melodic-Chemistry127
comments.body: You can't host an agent that will do any reasonable work for you on an 3060 Ti. If you have $20 to test things out, get a Claude Pro subscription, install Claude Code and let it guide you through everything. It will do a better job than any of us can do. Also, consider using Godot instead of Unity.

replies.author: One-Fall9946
replies.body: I still want to try the self hosted option. If that fails I will then try Claude.

comments.author: prayformcjesus
comments.body: Try magnitude but honestly your gpu is pretty weak for self hosted
